messages:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a speculative-sampler sketch (branching-sampler v1) on llama3-70b-quant4 w/ late-prefetch patch. long-form prompts (>1k tokens) show weird repetition/truncation around 800-900 tokens, looks like an abrupt falloff. attaching quick logs.

alex: can you paste the exact command and params? :mag:

maria: sure — ran on a small local node, command below:
```
./run_infer --model llama3-70b-quant4 \
  --sampler branching-sampler-v1 \
  --speculative True \
  --spec-branch-k 2 --temp 0.7 --top_p 0.95 \
  --prefetch late --kv-window 1024 --input-file longform_prompts.jsonl
```

devon: what's the batch/streaming config? kv-window 1024 is pretty large, any mem pressure? :thinking_face:

maria: batch=1 streaming=true. mem headroom was okay on the node. observed latency drop (~28% median token latency) vs baseline greedy path, so perf wins are real, but quality regressions on long tails.

jordan: do you have quantitative diffs? perplexity / human pref numbers?

maria: quick A/B (n=200 long-doc eval set):
- latency: -28% median token latency
- tokens per request: -18% (speculative prunes early)
- human-pref (pairwise): baseline beats spec 58% vs 42% (so ~16% relative drop)
- rouge-L: baseline 48.3 -> spec 46.9 (delta -1.4)

kevin: that's a non-trivial quality hit for long-form. Could be sampling-induced coherence breaks when speculative branch chooses higher-entropy continuation then fallback merges mismatch.

devon: my hunch: kv-cache alignment/eviction on quantized KV tensors. When speculative branch gets rolled back we might be re-inserting kvs with slightly different quantization noise causing decoder to drift for later tokens.

alex: idea: try running with deterministic-seed + dump-kv-checkpoints to compare raw KV activations between baseline and speculative runs at the rolloff point.

maria: tried deterministic seed and dumped kv slices for a failing prompt. diffs in kv quantized values are small but accumulate; after ~600 tokens divergence grows and you see repetition loops. attaching small excerpt log: "kv_chunk[23] quant_err_mean=0.0034, kv_chunk[23]_post_merge=0.0078"

jordan: can you repro on CPU quantized sim (to avoid GPU non-determinism)? if it's quant truncation accumulation that should show up.

maria: ran a CPU sim (toy) — accumulation still visible but smaller. also tried increasing kv-window to 2048 and it reduced early truncation but not eliminated. suspect subtle merge ordering + RNG interplay.

devon: other quick mitigations:
- increase fallback threshold (require higher confidence before committing spec branch)
- apply lightweight KL-penalty to prefer lower-entropy branch when merging
- re-quantize merged kvs w/ stochastic rounding to avoid bias

kevin: run plan suggestion: 1) reproducibility run w/ kv dumps (50 prompts), 2) ablation: speculative k=1 vs k=2, 3) eval full 500-longform holdout w/ human pairwise. schedule overnight.

maria: doing that. starting with k=1 and k=2 A/B now, tagging @devon @alex. will push kv dumps to s3: s3://redwood-ml/tmp/spec-kv-dumps/3460012345/

buildbot: job queued: run-3460012345-ablation started on node-ml-12 (ETA 2h)

alex: thanks — if the kv-merge is the culprit we should add an instrumentation counter in runtime for "merged_kv_delta_norm" so ops can alert when merge deltas exceed threshold.

maria: good call. will add metric and a quick smoke test to eng-ml canary once we have a fix.

kevin: also add a small human eval rubric: coherence, hallucination, structural integrity (headings/sections) for longform.

maria: noted. will share initial results in this thread when job finishes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
